Leading indicators

Track capability, adoption plans and commitments alongside the employment, productivity and scientific outcomes that follow. Each measure has its own coverage and reporting lag.

How to read these indicators

Leading signals describe capabilities, intentions or commitments that could precede wider economic effects. Broad proxies include non-AI activity. Confirmations measure realized outcomes; they can help establish whether earlier signals translated into change. Public sentiment measures stated views and expectations. None of these charts alone establishes an effect caused by AI.

The month selector limits observation dates, using the latest source versions and reviews. This is not a reconstruction of what was known in that month. Chart scales are independent; gaps are not filled and the last observation is not extended into the present. Reviewed snapshots require new source review to advance.

Survey coverage & updates

Surveys measure stated attitudes, not adoption, actual job losses or the tone of news coverage. Pew and Ipsos ask different questions and use different samples, so their percentages are not combined into a single sentiment score. Cross-country sample and age coverage also differ.

Each point links to a primary survey report, fieldwork dates and publication date. Charts use a fixed 0–100% scale. Missing waves remain missing. New survey releases require review before they are added; refreshing imports the reviewed catalogue. The month filter uses fieldwork dates with the latest reviewed evidence.

What counts

Registered human drug trials with a documented AI role in design, target selection, repurposing, recruitment or analysis. Roles can overlap; each registry ID counts once.

Results require a cited readout. A completed trial is not automatically a success, and a safety result does not establish efficacy.

Sources & definitions

AI sentiment

Pew tracks U.S. concern, excitement and expectations about jobs. Ipsos tracks attitudes across selected countries. Data-center surveys from Pew, Gallup, Ipsos and Annenberg cover local construction and perceived effects on communities. Each series retains its survey question, population, fieldwork dates and source report.

Charts use fieldwork dates and the latest reviewed evidence. Pew and Ipsos use different questions and samples; percentages remain separate. Ipsos history uses its 2026 report vintage. Missing survey waves remain gaps, and new releases require review.

Pew Research Center ↗ · Ipsos AI Monitor ↗

Jobs

Indeed’s share of postings mentioning AI-related terms, reported as a seven-day trailing average. Monthly changes compare the last observation in adjacent months, in percentage points.

Indeed methodology ↗

Labor-market context

The overlay offers a common starting index of 100 or normalization to each series’ own 0–100 range over the same time window. Flat series normalize to 50; original values remain available on hover. Indeed daily series use their last observation in each completed month; BLS and OECD series use their reference month. Gaps are preserved. The chart compares relative changes in different quantities, not job counts attributable to AI.

U.S. payrolls, unemployment, participation, openings, earnings, quits and layoffs come from BLS via FRED. Other countries include Indeed total postings and OECD harmonized unemployment via FRED. Age definitions and reporting lags differ.

Indeed total postings ↗ · FRED ↗

Supply chain

Federal Reserve, BLS and IMF series track chip output, transformer prices and copper. The Fed’s July 2026 compilation supplies memory prices, equipment investment, construction and selected cloud-firm capex. Ireland’s CSO supplies metered data-center power; Eurostat supplies EU enterprise AI adoption.

Geographies, units and frequencies stay separate. The Fed workbook is a dated compilation; other feeds refresh from their source. Annual adoption surveys have no 2022 observation, and the 2025 AI definition expanded. There is no additive total or estimate of AI’s causal contribution.

Fed data & definitions ↗

Medical devices

FDA-listed AI-enabled device submissions grouped by decision date and lead panel. Partial years are marked. Missing observations are not filled with zero.

FDA definitions ↗

AI in drug trials

Primary papers and sponsor disclosures document molecular design, target selection, repurposing, recruitment or trial analysis. Non-design entries are limited to individually verified trials; other trials of the same drug are not automatically included. Counts cover a reviewed catalogue, not the entire industry.

Actual trial starts anchor the activity series. Later AI analyses enter on their first documented report date; platform trials use the relevant drug-comparison start. Success counts require sourced primary efficacy results, with safety readouts counted separately. Mixed results and discontinuations remain visible. Outcomes do not establish that AI caused success. Registry status reflects the latest refresh.

ClinicalTrials.gov API ↗

Mathematical breakthroughs

News searches identify new results on famous conjectures and longstanding open problems. Each displayed result links to news or public expert coverage and the underlying research or announcement. Several articles about the same result count once; related bound families in one paper share an entry.

Counts describe reported breakthroughs, including claims under review and partial advances. Re-proving or formalizing known mathematics and olympiad scores are excluded. Formal verification of a new discovery remains eligible. Dates refer to public announcements; status reflects the latest source review. Coverage is curated, not exhaustive.

Value-chain activity & EUV

Taiwan MOEA supplies monthly production indexes and shipment/inventory values. U.S. Census via FRED supplies manufacturing orders, shipments, inventory and backlog; EIA supplies electricity generation and sales. UN Comtrade supplies annual gross exports for 11 selected product and material categories across 12 reporting economies and areas.

Trade coverage varies by product and year. Material categories include non-semiconductor uses and do not identify shipments to chipmakers or EUV suppliers. Prices, revenue, investment, physical shipments and stocks have distinct units. EUV relationships and company histories are curated from primary filings; new company disclosures require review before inclusion. Plans are separate from completed events. Location markers do not measure factory output.

Taiwan MOEA ↗ · UN Comtrade ↗

Dates and revisions

The month selector limits observations and documented events by date. Sources update on different schedules. Historical values use the latest ingested source versions and may be revised. No observation means unavailable, not no progress.
